transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, I came in because my head’s been feeling kind of foggy. I’ve been making little mistakes in my client notes at work, and I’ll forget what I was just about to do. That’s not really like me, so I figured I should get it checked out.
Can you describe exactly what happens when you feel foggy? For example, do you have trouble remembering recent events, following conversations, or knowing where you are?

It’s mostly like I lose my train of thought. I’ll be about to do something and then forget what it was, or I’ll write up client notes and notice I made small mistakes I normally wouldn’t make. I wouldn’t say I don’t know where I am or anything like that—it’s more just this foggy, slowed-down feeling in my head.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have been feeling pretty down lately. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel kind of sad and flat.
Have you noticed if this foggy feeling tends to come on when you’re feeling particularly anxious or stressed, or does it seem to happen more when you're just feeling down or low?

It seems to happen more when I’m feeling low. I don’t really notice it as much from being anxious or stressed. It’s just like my head gets foggy, and then I make little mistakes in my notes or forget what I was about to do.
Have you noticed any worsening in your ability to think clearly or remember things over the past few months, or has it been more consistent with how you usually feel when you’re down?

It’s been more noticeable lately, yeah. When I’m down, my head just feels foggy, and I’ll forget what I was about to do or catch little mistakes in my client notes. That’s not really like me, so that’s part of why I came in.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring about everything, but things just don’t feel as enjoyable lately. I still do what I need to do, but I don’t get much out of it.
Have you experienced any days where it was hard to even get out of bed or take care of basic tasks because of how you were feeling emotionally or mentally?

Not usually to the point where I can’t get out of bed or anything. But I have been less reliable with details. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client documentation, and at home my wife’s been taking over some of the bills and scheduling because I’m missing things more than usual.

Do you feel that your difficulty concentrating or remembering things is significantly worse than it’s ever been before, to the point where it’s clearly interfering with your ability to do your job or manage your usual responsibilities?

Yeah, I’d say it is interfering some. At work I’ve been asking coworkers to double-check my client notes because I’m not trusting myself with the details. And at home, my wife has had to take over some of the bills and scheduling because I’m missing things more than I usually would.
How long have you been feeling this way emotionally and experiencing the foggy thinking and forgetfulness — have these been ongoing for at least two weeks, or have they come and gone over time?
It’s been going on for at least a few weeks. I’d say the low, guilty feeling and the foggy thinking have been hanging over me for about a month now.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking that happen even when you're not feeling down or emotionally low?

I think it mostly shows up when I’m feeling low. That’s when my head feels foggy, and I’m making little mistakes in my client notes or forgetting what I was about to do. I haven’t really noticed it happening the same way when my mood is okay.
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Yeah. I’ve been blaming myself a lot, especially about my tío. I keep thinking I should’ve called more or gone to see him sooner before he died. It just keeps replaying in my head, like I failed him as family.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory or concentration even during times in the past when your mood was relatively good?

Not really, no. When my mood’s been okay, I don’t remember having this kind of fogginess. What’s bringing me in now is that my head feels cloudy, and I’m making little mistakes in client notes or forgetting what I was about to do, and that’s not normal for me.
So far, would you say your memory and concentration problems only happen when you're feeling down, or have you had times when your mood was okay but you still had those issues?

It seems like it’s only when I’m feeling down. That’s when my head gets foggy, and I start making little mistakes in my client notes or forget what I was about to do. When my mood is okay, I don’t really notice it.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure or feel interested in most activities you used to enjoy, even things like watching your favorite shows, spending time with friends, or hobbies?

I’m not sure I’d say that. I still can enjoy things sometimes, but I haven’t really been paying close attention to whether I’m interested in most stuff or not. It’s more like… some days I just don’t feel up for much.
Have you lost interest or felt little pleasure in almost all activities, even the ones you used to enjoy most?
I’m not really sure it’s almost all activities. I’ve had times where I don’t feel like doing much, but I can’t say I’ve completely lost interest in everything I usually enjoy.
Have you had days where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
Yeah… lately I’ve been waking up with this heavy, kind of empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and flat for a lot of the day.
Have you felt that you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

I don’t think I can say it’s almost all activities. I’ve noticed I’m less motivated sometimes, but I still can get some enjoyment from things here and there. It’s not like everything feels completely pointless or empty.
